title: Automating quantum circuit optimization with AI agents
abstract: Compiling quantum algorithms for real devices involves hard optimization problems that can decide whether an algorithm runs at scale. We present a general method for solving such problems with AI agents, with every result certified. It builds on autoresearch loops, in which agents iteratively improve programs against a fixed evaluator and which have recently improved quantum cryptanalysis circuits, and adds two elements: a frozen, exact verifier certifies every result, and this verifier, together with the challenge around it, is built by an agent that formulates the problem with a researcher and validates the verifier against a solved case, deliberately broken solutions and published results before any solution exists. The method applies to any optimization problem whose solutions can be verified exactly and efficiently. We apply it to three compilation problems in quantum simulation, namely fermion-to-qubit encoding, Hamiltonian layout and unitary synthesis. In each, the agents improved substantially on published or standard constructions, reducing the cost being optimized by up to 73% at the largest sizes tested and outperforming a state-of-the-art optimizer for fermion-to-qubit encodings. Every submission is a program accompanied by its agent's notes, so the ideas behind each improvement are recorded in human-readable form; later agents built on them, and we describe them here. These results open the way to automated, certified discovery across quantum circuit design and beyond.
summary: This paper presents a novel, general framework using AI agents to solve hard optimization problems in quantum circuit compilation, ensuring all results are mathematically certified. By applying this method to tasks like fermion encoding and unitary synthesis, the authors achieve significant performance improvements over state-of-the-art methods. This work opens the door for automated, trustworthy discovery across quantum algorithm design.
main_problem: The paper addresses the hard optimization problems inherent in compiling quantum algorithms for real hardware, which determines if an algorithm can scale.
main_result: The proposed AI agent framework substantially improved circuit optimization across three tasks—fermion-to-qubit encoding, Hamiltonian layout, and unitary synthesis—by up to 73% compared to prior methods.
method: It introduces a general method using AI agents within a verifiable autoresearch loop, featuring a frozen, exact verifier to certify every proposed improvement.
model_or_system: The work applies to quantum circuits, specifically optimizing encodings for quantum simulation (fermion-to-qubit) and finding minimal gate sequences for unitary synthesis using CNOT and Rz gates.
key_observables: Pauli weight (for encoding), SWAP count (for layout), and CNOT count (for synthesis).
important_parameters: The size of the system (e.g., lattice size $L$ or number of qubits $n \le 4$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that the optimization problem's solutions can be verified exactly and efficiently by a classical verifier.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the two components: the verified autoresearch loop and the challenge-construction system. Figure 2 summarizes results across the three compilation challenges. Other figures detail circuit walks and polynomial rewriting.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the general framework (autoresearch loop + verifier). It then applies this framework to three specific compilation problems: fermion-to-qubit encoding, Hamiltonian layout, and unitary synthesis, detailing the optimization targets and results for each.
why_interesting: The rigorous, certified nature of the optimization process, which builds upon established quantum simulation techniques, provides a powerful, general tool for designing complex quantum circuits.
